newsitem.title: USA: Church marks legacy of Martin Luther King Jr..
newsitem.headline: Church marks legacy of Martin Luther King Jr..

text.p: Civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. was remembered as a spiritual man who struggled for justice during a commemorative service on Monday at the church where he first preached.
King's widow, Coretta Scott King, said his birthday, which was first celebrated as a national holiday 11 years ago, has become a day for community service across the country.

"In every major city, community volunteers are engaging in a wonderful variety of humanitarian service projects such as cleaning up polluted streams, renovating shelters for the homeless, delivering meals to people with AIDS and teaching people how to read," Mrs. King said during a 2 1/2-hour service at Ebenezer Baptist Church.
"Today is not merely a holiday, but a true holy day which honours the life and legacy of Martin Luther King Jr., in the best possible way," she said.

The Rev. Randel Osburn, administrator of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference which King founded, used the occasion to call on the government to provide fewer subsidies to large corporations at the expense of the poor.
"Welfare reform is needed, but it ought to be started at the top," Osburn said.

Many politicians and dignitaries who usually attend the commemorative service, including King Centre president Dexter King, were in Washington on Monday for the inauguration of President Bill Clinton.
